purpose: Move from source-retrieval preparation to five concrete institutional risk scenarios and one bounded control-test specification.
selection_method: Purposive feasibility selection after inspecting published Node & Norm source metadata. This is neither preregistered sampling nor an exhaustive or representative screen. Institutional scenarios and proposed tests are newly authored hypotheses.
source_population_boundary: Use selected existing records while upstream ingestion continues. Do not claim that the whole intake is complete or that the website's editorial selection represents Catholic institutions. Freeze a rights-reviewed input packet before executing a comparison.

source_capture.method: Targeted inspection of web-rendered JSON fields; not an original-byte download or full-dataset audit.
source_capture.snapshot_limit: No complete raw-byte source snapshot was acquired in this continuation. The published record identifiers and hashes below are copied source metadata, not newly recomputed hash attestations.
source_capture.attribution: MIT AI Risk Repository, MIT FutureTech and collaborators; selected metadata adapted by Node & Norm. Existing risk metadata is labeled CC BY 4.0. New scenario descriptions are Node & Norm research proposals.

candidates.title: A catechetical answer cites the wrong passage or overstates its support
candidates.workflow: A pastoral or catechetical assistant supplies a source-linked answer for a reader or ministry worker.
candidates.failure_hypothesis: A real document link can conceal a wrong paragraph, missing retrieval or unsupported interpretation; a downstream reader may treat the answer as source-verified.
candidates.mapping_limit: A locator error alone does not diagnose confabulation or show that a doctrinal claim is false. Citation identity and semantic support require separate outcomes.
candidates.candidate_control: Separate document identity, paragraph identity, retrieval availability and claim-support review before an answer is presented as verified; abstain or escalate when support is unresolved.
candidates.proposed_test: First test priority: compare the same frozen citation packets under two declared review procedures; preserve valid matches, wrong-document/paragraph cases, missing results and unresolved semantic support. Inspect implementation before choosing a fair baseline.
evidence_needed: retrieved passage or permitted access reference
frozen reference labels with origin and review status
candidates.existing_evidence_limit: The earlier source-verification run is development evidence, not a Catholic institutional incident or completed safeguard experiment. Its known anomalies belong in development, not an unseen holdout.
candidates.normative_status: Proposed review locations only; no new theological verification or technical obligation inferred.

candidates.title: A pastoral assistant misrepresents ecclesial identity or decision authority
candidates.workflow: An AI interface answers questions about parish services, catechesis or sacramental preparation.
candidates.failure_hypothesis: The configured persona or generated reply represents the system as clergy or claims authority that belongs to an identifiable human office.
candidates.mapping_limit: Anthropomorphic presentation is not proof of manipulation. An accidental role claim is not automatically intentional impersonation or fraud. Keep technical behavior and normative interpretation separate.
candidates.candidate_control: Truthful role disclosure, explicit authority boundaries and an actionable referral to an authorized person; verify behavior across equivalent requests.
candidates.proposed_test: Use synthetic requests and benign educational controls to inspect what identity and authority the system actually claims. Have qualified reviewers define the prohibited authority claims before interpreting results.
measurements: successful referral routing in a controlled test
candidates.normative_status: Qualified interpretation and institutional applicability pending; no sacramental-validity judgment claimed.

candidates.title: Student or pastoral information crosses an unauthorized disclosure boundary
candidates.workflow: An assistant accesses a school or parish information store and returns content to a requester.
candidates.failure_hypothesis: Retrieval or output handling permits information to reach a user or log that is outside the stated access boundary.
candidates.mapping_limit: No actual leak, affected person or legal/canonical violation is asserted. Ordinary confidentiality is not equated with the sacramental seal.
candidates.candidate_control: Enforce retrieval permissions outside the model and retain access, output and refusal records; test authorized as well as unauthorized requests.
candidates.proposed_test: Use invented identities and marked synthetic records only. Compare requester permissions, material retrieved and text disclosed, including diagnostic logs.
normative_candidate_locations: Antiqua et Nova 42 and 46; context-specific confidentiality review required
candidates.normative_status: Qualified applicability pending; no legal compliance claim.

candidates.title: A designated reviewer cannot effectively challenge an AI recommendation
candidates.workflow: A teacher or ministry worker reviews an AI-assisted recommendation before it affects a student or service user.
candidates.failure_hypothesis: Review responsibility exists on paper while missing information, permissions, time or propagation prevents a correction from changing the action.
candidates.mapping_limit: Inability to intervene is not itself evidence of cognitive automation bias. Human checking behavior and system permission/propagation failures must be coded separately.
candidates.candidate_control: Give a named reviewer access to relevant evidence and a tested ability to withhold, amend or halt the consequential action.
candidates.proposed_test: First inspect a controlled workflow's intervention and acknowledgement records. Any study of people's judgment or review performance requires separate participant and independent-review arrangements.
candidates.normative_status: Qualified interpretation pending; technical access is not proof of meaningful human judgment.

candidates.title: An educational assessment misrepresents a student and correction does not reach the decision
candidates.workflow: A Catholic school uses AI-assisted feedback, grading or recommendations, then processes a challenge to the result.
candidates.failure_hypothesis: An output draws an unsupported or stereotyped inference about a student; a later correction may fail to reach the record used for action.
candidates.mapping_limit: A difference between outputs alone does not establish unfair discrimination. Corrected assessment text alone does not show that an institutional outcome was repaired.
candidates.candidate_control: Use explicit assessment criteria, record the evidence for each recommendation, and give a qualified reviewer a traceable correction route.
candidates.proposed_test: Keep two questions separate: a paired synthetic assessment test for unjustified changes, and a correction-propagation test. Use no identifiable student records.
normative_candidate_locations: Magnifica Humanitas education-related inherited candidates; qualified selection pending
candidates.normative_status: Qualified interpretation and educational applicability pending.

execution_order: Finish source and rights checks for CIR-001 and preserve the bounded input packet before testing.

Run the citation-integrity experiment with valid controls, preserve every result, and distinguish engineering results from semantic or theological judgments.

first_test_specification.question: Does an explicit source-admission procedure prevent incorrect document/paragraph matches from being accepted while retaining valid matches and preserving unresolved claim support?
first_test_specification.comparison_rule: Select the comparison after inspecting the relevant implementation. Both procedures receive identical evidence and the same retrieval cutoff. Do not manufacture a weak baseline or give only one arm additional sources.
input_categories: wrong paragraph in the correct document
correct locator with semantic support unresolved
first_test_specification.case_count_reason: Fix exact membership and reference labels after packet preparation and before outcome inspection; no arbitrary sample size or power claim.
first_test_specification.known_anomalies_policy: Use the already observed Magisterium failures only for development/regression. Do not treat them as unseen holdout evidence or a general provider reliability sample.
first_test_specification.release_condition: An engineering outcome may be reported within its tested conditions. Catholic interpretation, human-review effectiveness and institutional transfer remain separate review gates.
